Click chemistry revolutionizes chemical biology due to its high efficiency, specificity, and mild reaction conditions.
CuAAC and SPAAC are the most popular click reactions for constructing stable triazole rings.
CuAAC involves reacting an alkyne with an azide to produce 1,4-disubstituted 1,2,3-triazoles with near-perfect yield.
SPAAC eliminates the need for Cu(I) catalyst, making it safer and bioorthogonal.
Click chemistry is widely used in cancer immunotherapy, antibody–drug conjugates, PROTACs, exosome modification, and photodynamic therapy.
The Bertozzi group developed SPAAC as an alternative to CuAAC to avoid Cu(I) toxicity.
Bioorthogonal click chemistry allows selective labeling and tracking of biomolecules in living organisms.
Click chemistry enables rapid creation of extensive compound libraries with diverse biological activities.
The reaction can occur in water, facilitating its use across numerous research fields.
Click-activity-based protein profiling (click-ABPP) platforms help identify disease-relevant enzymes and develop selective pharmacological probes.
SPAAC is used to monitor azidosugars, proteins, lipids, and specifically labeled proteins, DNA, and RNA in living cells.
The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) estimated 20 million cancer cases and 9.7 million deaths globally in 2022.
IARC projects 35 million cancer cases globally by 2050.
Current cancer treatments often result in undesirable side effects and drug resistance.
Many anti-cancer drugs lack the ability to differentiate between healthy and cancerous cells, leading to toxicity in normal cells.
Click chemistry is used to develop novel Pt-based anticancer drugs by functionalizing them with biomolecules to enhance tumor targeting.
Click chemistry enables the attachment of targeting agents, delivery systems, fluorescent markers, and secondary chemotherapeutic molecules.
ADCs leverage the precise targeting capabilities of antibodies with the potent cell-killing effects of drugs.
More than 100 ADC candidates are undergoing clinical trials.
Click chemistry reduces production costs and minimizes toxic waste in ADC synthesis.
PROTACs are hetero-bifunctional molecules designed to facilitate target protein disposal by recruiting the ubiquitin-proteasome system.
Click chemistry allows for the modular assembly of PROTACs under near-physiological conditions.
Folate-conjugated PROTACs enhance tissue selectivity towards cancer cells and minimize toxicity in normal tissues.
Click chemistry facilitates the functionalization of exosomes with targeting ligands, improving their therapeutic efficacy.
Triazole derivatives can form varied non-covalent interactions with proteins, enzymes, and receptors, making them promising for anticancer drug development.
